9.	The most-influential law review article ever written was by future US Supreme Court justice Louis Brandeis and his law-firm partner Samuel Warren. They wrote “The Right to Privacy” in _Harvard Law Review_ in December 1890. The article argued for the legal recognition of “the right to be let alone.” Future Supreme Court justices cited this same right to privacy in landmark rulings like _Roe v. Wade_. The article itself was directly prompted by the release of a new small, portable hand-held Y in 1888 by the company X. The advertising slogan for the Y was: “You press the button, we do the rest.” Within a few years, beach resorts in the United States and Britain had banned Ys from their boardwalks; the Washington Post was warning its readers about predatory “Y fiends” stalking parks; the New York Times was running editorials about the loss of personal dignity in public spaces. ID X (5 points) and Y (5 points).
